title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Chen
body:
Purpose

This document is the canonical company handbook reference for working at Redwood Inference. It summarizes how we organize roles and career ladders, the benefits and perks available to employees, the hiring and onboarding experience, and the primary internal tools new hires and managers should understand. Use this as the single-pane summary for people-ops, hiring managers, and new employees; link to detailed policy pages where appropriate.

1) Quick summary

- Audience: new hires, hiring managers, people-ops partners, and people managers.
- Owner: People Ops (policy and maintenance).
- Last updated: 2025-08-01.

2) Working at Redwood — company values and expectations

Redwood is an engineering-first, product-driven organization. Our core values shape day-to-day work:

- Craftsmanship: shipping durable, well-tested systems.
- Empathy: prioritize customer and teammate outcomes.
- Pragmatism: measure impact and choose the simplest path that scales.
- Reliability: build observability and safety into products.

Expectations for every Redwood employee:

- Communicate asynchronously first; use meetings sparingly and with clear agendas.
- Write clear PRDs and design notes for cross-functional work.
- Follow the code review standard: at least one review from an owner and one from a domain expert.

3) Roles & career ladders (overview)

This section summarizes the role families and high-level leveling approach. Detailed competency matrices and promotion processes live in People Ops -> Career Ladders pages.

Role families (high level):

- Engineering: IC (E1–E5), Senior/Staff/Principal (E4–E6+), Eng Managers (M1–M3).
- Product: PM1–PM4, Senior PM, Group PM.
- Research/Applied ML: R1–R4, Senior Researcher, Research Manager.
- Platform & SRE: P1–P4, Senior/System Architect.
- GTM: Sales, Marketing, Customer Success levels.

High-level leveling summary (IC engineering):

- E1 (New grad / early entry): Contributes to a single component, receives mentorship.
- E2 (Engineer): Owns small features, participates in design.
- E3 (Senior Engineer): Drives medium-complexity projects, mentors juniors.
- E4 (Staff Engineer): Leads cross-team technical initiatives, shapes architecture.
- E5 (Principal / Distinguished): Organization-wide technical leadership.

Promotion process (brief):

1. Employee prepares a promotion packet with evidence mapped to competencies.
2. Manager reviews and adds assessment.
3. Calibration panel (peers + people-ops) reviews and decides.
4. Feedback and next steps communicated within two weeks of decision.

4) Benefits & perks (summary)

Redwood offers a competitive package designed to support employee wellbeing and productivity. Below is a concise summary — refer to Benefits Portal for full contracts and enrollment instructions.

Core benefits:

- Health insurance: three plans (PPO, HMO, High-deductible + HSA). Company covers 80% of premiums for employee; dependents at subsidized rate.
- Dental & vision: employer-sponsored dental plan and VSP vision plan.
- Parental leave: 18 weeks primary caregiver paid leave, 8 weeks secondary caregiver paid leave; flexible return-to-work options.
- Retirement: 401(k) with 4% company match for eligible employees.
- Equity: annual refresh grants for managers and ICs above E3, initial RSU package at offer.
- Commuter & wellness stipend: monthly allowance or remote-work equipment stipend.

Perks and programs:

- Learning stipend: $1,000/year for courses or conferences.
- Home office setup: $500 onboarding allowance + ergonomics support.
- Flexible PTO: manager-approved time-off policy with recommended minimum 15 days/year.
- Regular company offsites and team retreats (budgeted per team).

How to enroll and contacts (short):

- Benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood-internal (see People Ops > Benefits page).
- Questions: benefits@redwood.com or people-ops Slack channel (#people-ops).

5) Hiring & onboarding overview

This section outlines the standard hiring experience and the first 90-day onboarding structure used across engineering and product. Specific teams may add role-specific onboarding.

Hiring stages (standardized):

1. Resume screen and hiring manager phone screen (30–45 min).
2. Technical / role-focused interview loop (usually 3–4 interviews).
3. Hiring manager + team match / bar raiser conversation.
4. Offer decision and compensation calibration with People Ops.
5. Offer letter, background check, and start-date confirmation.

Interview best practices for hiring managers:

- Use the standardized rubric in People Ops; map to competencies required for the role.
- Provide candidate feedback within 48 hours of the loop.
- Coordinate with recruiting to define clear interview kits and reading materials.

Onboarding 30-60-90 (recommended plan)

- Day 0–7 (Orientation): HR paperwork, equipment delivered, account provisioning, first-week 1:1 with manager, team lunch.
- Week 2–4 (Foundations): Complete core trainings (security, privacy), read core product docs, shadow teammates, first small-ticket ownership.
- Month 2 (Integration): Deliver first small project or feature, present learnings to the team, schedule cross-functional meet-and-greets.
- Month 3 (Impact): Own a measurable piece of work aligned to quarterly goals, start career conversation and calibration with manager.

Onboarding checklist (example, use as a template):

1. Complete paperwork and tax forms.
2. Provision laptop and access to internal tools (see tools section below).
3. Complete security and privacy training (SLA: within 7 days).
4. Join team channels and set up recurring 1:1s with manager.
5. Deliver first small PR or documentation update within 30 days.

6) Internal tools guide (high level)

Redwood maintains a small set of core internal tools. New hires should be provisioned for these during Day 0 and complete the short orientation for each. Below are the primary tools, purpose, and quick-start steps.

- Code hosting: GitHub Enterprise (org: redwood-inference).
  - Access: request via onboarding forms; SSO through Okta.
  - Quick commands: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/<repo>.git; make test; make ci-check.

- CI/CD: Buildkite for internal pipelines and a gated release pipeline into production.
  - Owners: Eng Platform.
  - Quick start: view pipelines at https://buildkite.redwood-internal, open PR with branch naming convention 'team/short-desc'.

- Documentation: Confluence (this space) + docs-site (public-facing).
  - Confluence pages: use templates for runbooks and PRDs; all docs should have an owner and last-updated date.

- Chat & async comms: Slack (primary), with channels for teams and cross-functional flows. Use threads for context.

- Issue tracking & roadmaps: Linear for sprint work and roadmap planning.

- Observability: Datadog (metrics, logs) + Honeycomb (traces) for production systems.

- Customer data & CRM: Salesforce + secure data access via RBAC and internal dashboards.

Tooling access escalation procedure:

1. New hire unable to access a tool raises an incident in #oncall-and-incident-response via Slack and opens a ticket in the IT queue.
2. IT triages within 4 business hours. If not resolved, manager escalates to People Ops for temporary access.

7) Manager playbook (first 30 days of a new hire)

Manager responsibilities during onboarding:

- Week 0: schedule 1:1 cadence, set clear first-week goals, introduce to team and stakeholders.
- Week 1: perform a systems tour (architecture, codebase, deployments), ensure access to necessary repos and dashboards.
- Week 2–4: assign an early ownership task, schedule weekly feedback check-ins, and introduce performance review timelines.

Template 30-day goals for managers to share with new hire:

- Understand the primary code path and deployment flow for the owned service.
- Contribute a documentation improvement or small bug fix.
- Meet 8–10 cross-functional partners.

8) Promotion and compensation cadence

- Performance reviews: bi-annual formal reviews (mid-year and year-end) plus ongoing calibration conversations.
- Merit cycles: once per year aligned to fiscal budgeting; spot bonuses for exceptional contributions may be awarded throughout the year.
- Promotion windows: rolling but typically finalized during calibration windows; employees are encouraged to discuss readiness with managers at least one cycle prior.

9) Security, privacy, and compliance expectations for all employees

- Complete mandatory security and privacy training within 7 days of start.
- Use the company-approved password manager and enable MFA on all accounts (Okta + hardware token for privileged access).

10) Common FAQs (short)

Q: Who do I contact about payroll or benefits?
A: benefits@redwood.com or People Ops Slack.

Q: Where are team-specific onboarding checklists stored?
A: In Confluence under each team space and in the Onboarding template gallery.

Q: How do I request a conference or learning budget?
A: Use the learning stipend request form (link in People Ops page). Approvals take 3–5 business days.

11) Useful links and references

- People Ops > Career Ladders (detailed competency matrices).
- Benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood-internal.

- Onboarding templates: Confluence templates -> Onboarding.
- Security training: internal training portal -> security.

12) Governance, reviews, and updates

- Owner: People Ops (document owner).
- Review cadence: annual review or on major policy changes (compensation, benefits, legal).
- Change process: open a PR against this Confluence page and add reviewers; People Ops will coordinate final approval with Finance/Legal where required.

Appendix A: Example onboarding checklist (copyable)

1) HR: complete W-4/contract and personal info.
2) IT: laptop assignment, SSO and GitHub access.
3) Security: complete privacy and security training.
4) Manager: schedule 1:1 cadence and define first 30-day project.
5) Team: intro meeting, runbook overview, and deploy walkthrough.

Appendix B: Example git quickstart

- Clone: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/example-service.git
- Build: make build
- Test: make test
- Open PR: gh pr create --base main --title "<short desc>" --body "Summary and testing notes"

Contact and escalation

For policy clarifications or to report missing information, open a People Ops ticket or email people-ops@redwood.com. For security incidents during onboarding, contact security@redwood.com and follow the incident response runbook.

End of document.
